blocks.text: The judicial chronicle and the administrative texts have a very precise Arabic: each word has a technical value, and an approximate translation ('condemned' by 'defendant', 'final judgment' by 'first-degree judgment') changes the meaning of the news. In this unit you learn the vocabulary of courts and of the stages of a trial as the press tells you, the language of regulatory texts (articles of law, "is forbidden" , "is allowed," "except"), the vocabulary of administrative documents and practices and the rules of prudence to report a judicial case (presumption of innocence, attribution). The cases of the texts are invented and concern only civil and administrative matters or public events told by the newspapers. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-13.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. understand a judicial news: courts, parties, stages of the trial, types of judgment, appeals;
2. a precise distinction between accused and convicted, first and final judgment, prosecution and evidence, and
to report them in compliance with the presumption of innocence;
3. read an article in law or regulation: numbering, obligations, prohibitions, exceptions, entry into force;
4. understanding the vocabulary of documents and administrative practices (release, renewal, legalization, appeal);
5. read a judicial or administrative service of 350 words at least 80 words per minute.

a) The Administrative Court; the decision of the municipality to close the old weekly centre market; and

transfer it to an industrial area in the suburbs; on appeal by the association of market traders (case brought six months earlier). Legal basis: Article 18 the law on public markets, which obliges local authorities to consult the traders concerned before transferring an active market for more than ten years. The municipality had invoked safety and traffic reasons on the basis of a technical report on road congestion; the court replied that those legitimate reasons do not exempt from the obligation of consultation. It is not definitive: the municipality can resort to the supreme administrative court within the legal deadline, sixty days after notification. Forms of law: ⁧ينص عليها القانون⁩ · ⁧تلزم السلطات المحلية بـ⁩ (also ⁧أحكام القضاء⁩ , ⁧الأجل القانوني⁩ ). Attribution verbs: ⁧جاء في⁩ · ⁧رحب⁩ · ⁧قال⁩ · ⁧أعلنت⁩ · ⁧أضاف⁩ · ⁧يرى⁩ .
b) Over a million cases are delayed, some of which last for years (as estimated by the Ministry of Justice). Digitisation

allows cases and memories to be filed, pay online fees and hold certain hearings at a distance; the Ministry claims that it has reduced some procedures from weeks to days and saved expensive travel. Objections: remote hearings can harm the rights of the defence (difficult to evaluate a witness from a screen, difficult for the accused to communicate freely with the lawyer); some citizens (older people, rural areas) have no skills or devices; protection of very sensitive data. Solution proposed by some judges: combining paper and screen, digitizing administrative procedures and maintaining in presence the hearings that require direct listening. Final phrase: Slow justice is an injustice, but rapid justice without guarantees is not justice. Opinions: Ministry ( ⁧تؤكد⁩ ), some lawyers ( ⁧يرى بعضهم⁩ · ⁧يشير آخرون⁩ ), some judges ( ⁧كما يقترح⁩ ); the author in the last paragraph ( ⁧يبدو أن⁩ · the final sentence).
